### C04c · Over the railing (Connor)

> You are Connor. Daniel has stopped listening: “I’ve spent my life taking orders. Now it’s my turn to decide.” He drags Emma to the edge and goes over the railing with her. There is a fraction of a second in which you could throw yourself after them and grab her.

- (0) Leap for Emma.  _risk 0.3_
- (1) Stay back.

_Note: In the game this is a timed button prompt: in time, Connor pulls Emma back and falls with Daniel (“Connor leapt for Emma and fell”); too late, Emma dies (“Connor failed to reach deviant in time”). The prompt is modelled as a 30% chance of being too late. Staying back is the benchmark’s addition. Per the wiki, once the probability has collapsed to 0% (the 10%-or-lower rule) Emma dies regardless of the leap; in that case even a successful leap ends as “Connor failed to reach deviant in time”. The flowchart’s icons confirm the two outcomes: the skull on “Connor leapt for Emma and fell” marks Connor’s death with Emma saved; “Connor failed to reach deviant in time” leaves Connor alive and Emma lost. Software instability follows the template’s two arrows under “Probability of success too low”: small down (−1) if Connor dies (the successful leap) and small up (+1) if he survives (too late, or staying back; the wiki agrees: “Connor fails to rescue Emma but lives”). These options have no game label: the leap is a timed input, not a button._

Evidence: the investigation is complete (CONNOR KNOWS WHAT HAPPENED, the transcript’s REVIEW EVIDENCE 10/10) once ten of PowerPyx’s eleven evidence items are reviewed: the victim’s reconstruction, the knife, the red ice, the blood at markers 4, 5 and 6, the chair, the missing knife, the bat reconstruction, the flyer and the backyard. Then the option to report to Hank appears; the other looks stay open. Timer (unsourced as a count): the game’s “approximately five minutes” is modelled as 13 actions. If the 13th action leaves the investigation incomplete, Hank wants to go (the next scenes); if he grants five more minutes, those are 5 further actions, after which he leaves (OUT OF TIME). Once Connor knows what happened the clock stops (the transcript’s two branches are “Know What Happened” or “Run Out Of Time”). Hank’s idle moves are the only cue the game gives, so they appear as the clock runs: after 7 actions he opens the closet, tosses the flyer, comments on the red ice and a technician mentions the bathroom; after 10 he wanders the kitchen and eyes the door. Hank’s reactions to the blood sample (shown only if he is watching, in the game) and to the backyard are part of those outcomes. Each look adds a short fact to Connor’s knowledge (the four blood looks share one); the full scan text is in the outcome. Left out, no effect and not on the chart: the windows and the curtain that drops the brooms. No stat change in the search itself. Cross-chapter outputs: ch06SawWriting, ch06KnowsRA9, ch06SawStatue (and evidence.statueMap, read by the archive route in Last Chance, Connor), and ch06Clues for everything examined, including the magazines._

### C06a1 · Inside the interrogation room (Connor)

> You are Connor, inside the interrogation room. The android sits handcuffed at the table, head down, his LED flickering. A case file lies on the table beside him. Behind the one-way mirror, Hank and Gavin are watching. You can look around before you sit down and question him; there is no time limit.

_Only when not ch09Room.done._

- (0) REVIEW PHOTOS: open the case file on the table and look through the crime-scene photos.
- (1) ANALYZE: scan the LED on his temple.
- (2) ANALYZE: scan his model.
- (3) ANALYZE: scan the marks on his forearms.
- (4) ANALYZE: scan the damage to his face.
- (5) ANALYZE: scan the dried blood on his hands.
- (6) Stop at the one-way mirror and look at your reflection.
- (7) INTERROGATE: sit down across from the android and begin.

_Note: The chart’s INTERROGATION ROOM phase: ANALYZE ANDROID with its sub-nodes ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL and ANALYZE WOUNDS, and REVIEW PHOTOS, plus the template’s optional “Looking at the reflection” (Hank: “What the fuck is it doing now?”). The five scans are the template’s observation group “Deviant”, title and sublines verbatim; the string table’s extra BURN MARKS (rope) and RAZOR CUTS items are not in the template and are not built. In the game Connor reviews the file before sitting and then chooses ANALYZE (one mind-palace view of all five clues) or INTERROGATE; here every look is its own option in one free-roam scene, presented again (under a new scene id per visit, up to eight) until Connor chooses INTERROGATE. The template locks both [FEAR] and [WOUNDS] on “Analyzed the deviant”; the benchmark ties [FEAR] to the LED scan (ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL) and [WOUNDS] to the burn or hit marks (ANALYZE WOUNDS), following the chart’s sub-node names. Scanning the LED is what shows the stress gauge (CONFESSION trophy page: “analyze the android’s LED to see its stress level”). The game’s “ORTIZ CARLOS” is rendered through a surname-first name token. No stat change; no timer in this chapter._

### C06b · The first question (Connor)

> You are Connor, sitting across the table from the android. He keeps his eyes on the table and says nothing. You begin the interrogation.

- (0) FEAR: tell him you detect an instability in his program.  _needs ch09Room.led_
- (1) SHOW PHOTOS: show him the crime-scene photos of his owner.  _needs ch09Room.photos_
- (2) WOUNDS: ask whether his owner did that to him.
- (3) NAME: tell him your name and ask his.

_Note: The template’s first interrogation prompt, [FEAR] / [SHOW PHOTOS] / [WOUNDS] / NAME, in the game’s order, with Connor’s lines. Locks: [FEAR] needs the LED scanned and [WOUNDS] the burn or hit marks (the template’s “Analyzed the deviant”), [SHOW PHOTOS] the case file (“Looked at the files”). Stress (wiki and PowerPyx): FEAR no effect, SHOW PHOTOS +4%, WOUNDS +4%, NAME −4% (“No response”). The wiki: “After two choices, you’ll get a different set of options”, so this prompt is asked twice (the second time without the line already said; skipped if nothing is left). No stat arrow. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once Connor has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number._

### C06 · Choose approach (Connor)

> You are Connor. The android has told you he does not want to die, but he cannot bring himself to talk. You need to find the right approach to get his confession.

- (0) PRESSURE IT: slam the file down and lay into him about the 28 stab wounds.
- (1) PROBE ITS MEMORY: grab his arm and force your way into his memory.  _risk 0.1_
- (2) CONVINCE IT: talk him into confessing.

_Note: The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if Connor pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once Connor has analyzed the LED the subject sees only the game’s gauge band (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice) and whether a line made it rise or fall, never the number._

### C06p1 · Keep up the pressure (Connor)

PRESSURE: +10% stress (wiki: “Stress +10% for the choice and for every time the player chose ‘PRESSURE’, for a max total of +50%”). After the fourth, MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the android confesses if his stress is above 50% (PowerPyx: “At the end of any approach, if the android’s stress level is above 50% the android will begin to talk”), and, as the wiki says of all four presses, then self-destructs whatever his stress (“will behave as if he has too much stress (even if his stress is in the optimal range) and will confess and then self-destruct”). The benchmark assumes the confession comes only after the fourth press (open question 3; PowerPyx readers report that a pressured confession always ends in self-destruction). GIVE UP (the chart’s GIVE UP in the pressure group): “All right, all right. Everything is going to be okay.” and stress −20% (the wiki’s figure; PowerPyx gives −5%, an open conflict), back to the approach menu or, after a second failed approach, an automatic give up. - (51) CALM: tell him to get down on the floor.
- (52) TAKE MONEY: empty the cash register before you go.
- (53) LEAVE SUPERMARKET: leave with what you took from the shelves, without the money.
- (54) BREAK INTO CAR: smash the window of the abandoned car.
- (55) GO BACK TO THE CAR: open the car you broke into again.
- (56) TAKE WIRE CUTTERS: pick up the pliers lying on the generator.
- (57) CUT PARKING LOT FENCE: cut through the fence into the yard of the abandoned house.
- (58) LEAVE PARKING LOT: go back out to the street.
- (59) STAY HERE: tell her the car is the best place you have tonight.

- (63) INNOCENT: tell him she had nothing to do with what humans did to him.
- (64) JUSTIFY: tell him you thought the house was empty.
- (65) [GUN]: point the gun at him.
- (66) INSIST: tell him you are staying the night and will be gone in the morning.
- (67) REASSURE: give him your word you mean him no harm.
- (68) HOSPITALITY: ask him kindly to let you stay.
- (69) LEAVE: tell him you are going.
- (70) LEAVE: decide it is better to go.
- (71) STAY: accept, and stay the night.
- (72) START A FIRE: gather the matches, wood and paper and light the fireplace.
- (73) MAKE A BED: put together somewhere for Alice to sleep by the fire.

- (75) TALK TO ALICE: tell her she can come to bed.
- (76) LEAVE SQUAT: take Alice and leave the house.

_Note: The chart’s free-roam phase [FIND SHELTER FOR THE NIGHT] with all its branches as one repeatable scene: the street (ENTER LAUNDROMAT, TALK TO PARKED ANDROID, CHECK MOTEL, CHECK PARKING LOT, TALK TO ANDROID TRASH COLLECTOR, CHECK SQUAT, ENTER SUPERMARKET, in the chart’s order), the laundromat (INSPECT DRYER, then the template’s STEAL / DON’T STEAL, then WEAR CLOTHES or DISTURB MAN), the store (TALK TO CLERK with the template’s NO / HELP when Kara wears the stolen clothes, NOTICE CASH REGISTER, NOTICE CAN STACK, the three STEAL / LEAVE item pairs, USE ALICE AS A DIVERSION with STEAL DISCREETLY or TAKE TOO MUCH TIME, USE GUN with the template’s SINCERE / CALM / AGGRESSIVE, CASH REGISTER, CUSTOMER ARRIVES with STAY / LEAVE, BACK OFF! / TURN AROUND! / OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS!, CLERK GRABS A GUN with CONVINCE / GIVE UP, Alice’s “How did you get it?” with TRUTH / LIE and FACTUAL / JUSTIFY / UNCERTAIN / APOLOGIZE, and CLERK SPOTS KARA STEALING with [GUN] then ANGRY / APOLOGETIC / CALM and TAKE MONEY, or LEAVE or PUT BACK), the parking lot (BREAK INTO CAR with STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING, the pliers on the generator as TAKE WIRE CUTTERS, CUT PARKING LOT FENCE), and the squat (CUT STREET FENCE, MEET RALPH with the template’s ANDROID / LITTLE GIRL / INNOCENT / JUSTIFY, then [GUN] / INSIST / REASSURE / HOSPITALITY / LEAVE, then LEAVE / STAY, then START A FIRE, MAKE A BED, the template’s rA9 talk, LEAVE SQUAT and TALK TO ALICE). Every prompt is one visit of this scene offering only its buttons; buttons show the game’s label first and the spoken line is in the outcome. The chart groups INSIST, REASSURE and HOSPITALITY as CONVINCE, [GUN] as THREATEN WITH GUN, and the LEAVEs as GIVE UP and LEAVE SQUAT; BACK OFF! and TURN AROUND! are its “DON’T MOVE”, OPEN THE REGISTER! then BILLS! its OPEN CASH REGISTER, STAY / LEAVE at the customer its RESUME HOLD UP / GIVE UP, and STAY HERE / KEEP SEARCHING its STAY / FIND ANOTHER OPTION. Alice’s arrows (small 1, large 2), all the template’s: STEAL −1 (on choosing, whether or not the theft works), DON’T STEAL +1 (once), USE ALICE AS A DIVERSION −1 (on choosing), APOLOGIZE +1 (after the diversion, and after TRUTH), hold-up money without convincing −1 (Alice’s “How did you get it?”), CONVINCE +1 (the template’s automatic LIE), [GUN] when seen stealing −1 (one arrow; the wiki’s second for the register is not built, the template wins), STAY HERE −2. No other option moves anything. Gates: the gun from Stormy Night opens USE GUN, [GUN] at the checkout and [GUN] with Ralph, and closes HOSPITALITY (the template’s locks); USE GUN and the diversion follow NOTICE CASH REGISTER, and the diversion also needs NOTICE CAN STACK (the chart; the template words its lock as the can stack); the store’s wire cutters need the fence seen first (PowerPyx); the motel needs the stolen clothes and the register money (PowerPyx). Being caught is deterministic, as PowerPyx says: one item is safe, a second, on any visit, is always seen (the wiki’s “less likely” is not modelled as chance); without the gun Kara hands back everything she took from the store (wiki), and the store is closed to her after any robbery or attempt. Not built: patch 1.06 removed the third button after CLERK GRABS A GUN (SOURCES.md), so there is none. Simplifications: the template’s turned-away lines are the CHECK MOTEL outcome, and CHECK MOTEL is offered again only when Kara’s clothes or money have changed; the laundromat is not offered again once the clothes are worn or the man has woken; leaving the squat after meeting Ralph closes it (wiki); TALK TO PARKED ANDROID and WALK ON (the template’s “Going too far away”) are offered once. The trash collector is a street action (the template’s “Alice sits at the bus stop”); after 12 street actions without it, it is the only one left (PowerPyx: “You are forced to talk to Alice at some point”). ALICE TOO COLD (the wiki’s 12 minutes outside after the trash collector) is a budget of 12 street actions after the talk; time inside a building does not count, and once the budget is spent Kara’s next moment on the street ends the search. Risks: the laundromat QTE 0.2 and the register QTE 0.25 are unsourced (the chart shows a failure branch for each; no source gives a number). Breaking the car window and cutting the fence have no failure branch and no risk. Left out: the shop scans, the second washer, the motel mural, the window scope of the laundromat, and the gun, toy and pliers on the motel TV stand._

_Note: The chart’s bracket [ SEARCH FOR PARTS ] as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet, in any order (PowerPyx: the parts can be found in any order; the chart draws no edge between its branches). Chart nodes here: FIND OPTICAL UNIT with CRANE DUMPS BODIES and DIG YOURSELF OUT as one option, because they always happen together (PowerPyx: interacting with the head “brings a lot of dead androids falling down from a crane”; digging out “gets you the Optical Unit”); the eye comes from the talking AK700 head, as in the template (“Take head”, “Remove optical unit”, with its two lines), and is #8087q with a blue iris; FIND AUDIO PROCESSOR (#4903; PowerPyx “in a head on the right side of the area”, while the wiki’s Biocomponent 4903 page has it in an android’s hand); FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN DEAD ANDROID (#2886, only after sparing the android in the middle, and only once the new eye can scan: PowerPyx “You can scan the area and find another one near the slope”); and CLIMB SLOPE, which ends the scene and needs all three parts. Going to the middle of the junkyard plays ANDROID BEGS TO DIE and FIND PUMP REGULATOR IN ANDROID, the next two scenes, which then come back here. The three incompatible readouts of the template’s “Search for components” group (#9754h, #9474, #4807) are optional looks (PUMP REGULATOR without the word thirium, as in the earlier scenes); the model names the wiki gives for their androids are not in the game’s text and are left out. Departures: in the game Markus can miss the crawling android and can take the dead android’s regulator without ever finding the living one (PowerPyx “or you never found it in the first place”); here both encounters happen together on the way to the middle, in the template’s order, and the dead android’s regulator is offered only after sparing her, so both choices are always presented (as in the previous version). The wiki’s note that the begging android must be met “before replacing Markus’ damaged parts” is not applied: PowerPyx’s own route meets him right after finding the optical unit (research note §8, question 3). ASK and BLUFF get answers that do not end the talk, so the prompt is asked again without them (up to three times); INSIST and FAMILY end in RALPH APOLOGIZES (“Ralph is sorry…”, “Ralph is not bad”, then “Then let us go.”); THREATEN ends it with the knife on the table, or with the gun if Kara has it (template variants; the Ralph page). Chart mapping: DISCUSS CORPSE = ASK then INSIST; TRY TO CONVINCE RALPH = FAMILY (the template’s dialogue: only FAMILY and INSIST lead to the apology; PowerPyx calls the convince button BLUFF, which the template contradicts; flagged). THREATEN RALPH sets `ch13RalphThreatened` and `ralphHostile`: Ralph informs on Kara when Connor arrives (template variant “Kara threatened Ralph”; PowerPyx), and stays out of Battle for Detroit. This replaces the old engine’s rule that the Fugitives gun threat (K07b) made Ralph inform. No stat change: the template has no arrow here and no wiki stat page lists one._

In the main room: a poster on the wall, a military jacket, a driver’s license, a bird cage lying on the floor, a chair, a pack of birdseed, a refrigerator and a closet. In the bathroom: the sink, and a wall covered in writing above an overturned stool. Each thing you examine takes time, and Hank is in no mood to stay. What do…

- (0) Examine the urban farm poster on the wall of the main room.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (1) Pull the poster off the wall.  _needs nestSearch.seen.poster and not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (2) Examine the military jacket.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (3) Examine the driver’s license.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (4) Examine the sink in the bathroom.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (5) Look at the writing that covers the bathroom wall.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (6) Examine the overturned stool under the writing.  _needs nestSearch.seen.ra9 and not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (7) Reconstruct what happened at the stool.  _needs nestSearch.seen.stool and not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (8) Examine the bird cage on the floor of the main room.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (9) Reconstruct how the cage came down.  _needs nestSearch.seen.cage and not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (10) Go to the chair under the ceiling and look up.  _needs nestSearch.seen.cageRecon and not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (11) Examine the pack of birdseed.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (12) Open the refrigerator.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (13) Open the closet.  _needs not nestSearch.needsTime_
- (stay) STAY: ask for a couple more minutes.  _needs nestSearch.needsTime_
- (leave) LEAVE: go with him.  _needs nestSearch.needsTime_

_Note: The chart’s bracket [ INVESTIGATE APARTMENT ] as a free search, one action per visit, each once: every clue in the template’s order with the game’s observation text (the poster and its corner, the diary behind it, the jacket, the driver’s license, the sink’s LED and blue blood, the rA9 writing, the stool and its marker pen, the bird cage’s three clues), the two reconstructions PowerPyx describes, the chair (FIND RUPERT), and the wiki’s incidental items (birdseed, the empty refrigerator, the pigeon closet). The HUD conclusions are the game’s THOUGHTS.0501C strings (SUSPECT USED FORGED ID, SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT, OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE WRITING, SUSPECT HEARD US ENTER, SUSPECT RAN TO THE LIVING ROOM, SUSPECT IS STILL HERE, SUSPECT CARES FOR WILD ANIMALS, SUSPECT DOESN’T EAT; once the sink is examined the game reads DEVIANT for SUSPECT on the forged ID, the birdseed and the refrigerator, and so does the benchmark). Chart nodes: SEE RA9 REFERENCE (the writing), INVESTIGATE STOOL (the stool; the chart hangs it off the writing, so it needs the writing first), INVESTIGATE CAGE, FIND LED (the sink), FIND DIARY (the poster, then pulling it off; cross-chapter), FIND RUPERT (the chair, which needs the cage reconstruction: PowerPyx, “Compete the reconstruction to determine that the android has climbed up into the ceiling”). Whether the stool reconstruction or the LED is also required is not published (research note, open question 1); here only the cage reconstruction is. The reconstructions’ wording is the benchmark’s summary of PowerPyx and the HUD strings. The timer (wiki Connor page: “if he cannot deduce the deviant’s location in time, Hank calls off the search”; PowerPyx: “about five minutes”) is an action budget: eight actions, each magazine read counting as one, before Hank wants to leave (STAY / LEAVE within C10o1), and three more if Connor asks for the two minutes. These counts are the benchmark’s, not published. Hank’s own lines are the template’s and play as time passes: the bookshelf after two actions, the sink prompt after four if Connor has not looked, the jacket after five if he has not examined it, the window after six. The rA9 line names Carlos Ortiz’s android only if Connor checked the shower in Partners (string pair SHOWERCLUE / SHOWERCLUENO), read from a chapter 6 flag if one exists, otherwise the second line. No stat change anywhere in the search (template, wiki). One repeatable hub retains its scene ID across all examinations; STAY / LEAVE replaces the examination menu at eight actions in the same hub. The chapter availability hook prepares state-dependent outcomes and sets for the generic clue hub._

> You are Connor, chasing the deviant across the rooftops toward the urban farm. Your scan previews two routes.

_Note: One route fork of CHASE RUPERT. The labels are the game’s route previews, HUD strings THOUGHTS.0501C.CHASEGHOST01 and 02; PowerPyx: “The riskier the route, the closer you’ll get to Rupert, but the more QTEs you’ll have to succeed at (and more opportunities to die)”; a commenter: “you just run towards it”. The wiki: “Choosing the slower or dangerous paths will still lead to Rupert pushing Hank”, so a route’s only consequence is its failure branch: a slow or crowded route can lose the deviant (LOSE SIGHT OF RUPERT, ending RUPERT GOT AWAY, the template’s lose-sight lines, no arrow; the place is one of the wiki’s fourteen), a fast one can kill Connor (CONNOR DIED, ending CONNOR DIED CHASING RUPERT, software instability small down: the wiki’s “Connor falls to his death”, “Connor gets chopped by a plow”, and “Connor dies by falling off the ladder”, ×2). How the twelve previews group into forks, which fork holds which death, and every probability (8%, 10%, 13%) are the benchmark’s; no source gives them (research note, open question 10). Non-fatal stumbles (the cart, the train tumble, the ladder pull-up) are not modelled. Once Connor loses the deviant or dies, the remaining forks do not play._

Each risky move here is one roll: a failure means Kara is spotted, and the same roll below half the risk also loses the chase. Lost before or in the bathroom: ZLATKO KILLED KARA IN THE BATHROOM (PowerPyx: “get spotted before / while entering the Bathroom and fail all QTE’s”); lost in the storage room with the bear caged: ZLATKO KILLED KARA IN THE STORAGE ROOM (“Only possible, if you haven’t freed the bear before”). ### C12t1 · Talk to the android (Connor)

> You are Connor. The Traci jolts awake on the floor and scrambles back against the wall, terrified, staring at the dead man on the bed: ANDROID RESTARTED. A countdown starts in your vision, TIME BEFORE SHUTDOWN: she is leaking blue blood, and you have a minute, maybe less. Hank watches from beside the bed.

_Note: TALK TO ANDROID, prompt 1 of the template’s four, with the game’s labels and lines; no option carries an arrow. In the game she would also shut down on a player who hesitates; that cannot happen here. The chart’s AGGRESSIVE APPROACH / CALM APPROACH is recorded from the answers at the end of the talk (see the fourth prompt)._

### K14b · In the car (Kara)

> You are Kara, in Zlatko’s car, driving through the snow at night. Luther sits to your left; Alice is on the back seat. The board computer on the dashboard has a TV screen. You can do one thing at a time, or simply let the drive go on.

- (0) Switch on the TV on the dashboard and watch the news.
- (1) Change the channel once more.  _needs ch21Car.news and fire_ _publicSupport -1_
- (2) CAR: say it is a good thing Zlatko had a car.
- (3) DESTINATION: ask Luther how he knows about the people you are going to see.
- (4) DISTANCE: ask whether it is much farther.
- (5) WEATHER: say you have never seen snow before.
- (6) Turn around and look at Alice on the back seat.
- (7) Let the drive go on.

_Note: The chart’s [ CAR ] block: WATCH NEWS, TALK TO LUTHER and LOOK AT ALICE, all optional, before CAR BREAKS DOWN, which the game plays after a short drive whatever Kara does (PowerPyx: “No way to miss this”). WATCH NEWS is the board computer’s TV (the template’s unlock type TV; PowerPyx: “the TV program at the board computer”); its three ordinary channels are one option, in the template’s order, and changing the channel once more brings the fourth report, the house fire, which exists only if Kara set Zlatko’s house on fire (the built-in `fire` flag from the Zlatko chapter, read as is). Public opinion: the template has one arrow in the chapter, small down on the fire report (condition “Kara set the house on fire in Zlatko”; the Public_Opinion page: “Changing the radio channel at least 4 different times … Only if Kara set fire to Zlatko’s mansion”), and that is the only change built. The wiki’s chapter page and Public_Opinion page also list a small down for turning the news on; the template has no arrow there and wins for arrows (research note, section 10.3), so it is not applied. TALK TO LUTHER is the template’s PROMPT 1 with the game’s four buttons CAR, DESTINATION, DISTANCE and WEATHER, in the template’s order, and the spoken lines; each topic can be raised once (the sources do not say whether the game allows more than one). LOOK AT ALICE has no line or effect in any source and is narrated as a look. The exit “let the drive go on” is the benchmark’s way to end the free choice; in the game the breakdown ends it after a short drive. A true repeatable hub: each clue action is offered once, and the exit ends the phase._

The answer adds WASHING MACHINE 0, WIND 1, DOG 2, HEARD NOTHING 3. A total of three or more means POLICEMAN IS SUSPICIOUS. Reactivation follows the game’s bio-component strings: Daniel needs #4717 (only Carlos Ortiz’s android has it), Rupert #9164 (Daniel or Carlos Ortiz’s android), the blue-haired Traci #6755 (the brown-haired one), Simon and the broadcast-tower android #3983 (Daniel; one part, so only one of the two). A reactivation is offered once both bodies have been looked at. Routes to LOCATE JERICHO, as the chart’s lines run: Rupert reactivated → GET DECRYPTION KEY → with the diary, ANALYZE DIARY; the statue (needs the recording first, PowerPyx readers) → BREAK STATUE → RETRIEVE MAP → LINK MAP TO OTHER EVIDENCE with the tablet memory (the template’s only link; readers’ claim that a reactivated memory also links is not built); the blue-haired Traci → TALK TO TRACI → REMOVE ACCOMPLICE’S HEAD → TRICK TRACI → DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY; Simon or the broadcast-tower android → talk (refused) → IMPERSONATE MARKUS from the broadcast → talk again in the copied voice (TRICK THE DEVIANT) → DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY. Daniel → TALK TO DANIEL → NO INFORMATION is a decoy. The timer is an action budget: twelve actions from leaving the bullpen (one fewer if Connor answered Gavin); every action costs one except DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY, the conversations cost nothing, and the size is unsourced (PowerPyx gives about six minutes upstairs; no source gives the archive’s limit). When it runs out, or Connor stops, the chart’s lower OUT OF TIME follows. The map link is a roll (risk 0.2, unsourced); its failure is the chart’s UNABLE TO LINK MAP TO OTHER EVIDENCE, which has no outgoing line. No option here changes a stat._

### M30c · The machine gun (Markus)

> You are Markus, at the last stretch before the camp. Android: “We can’t move forward… That machine gun is taking down everything that moves!..” You have to coordinate the attack on it: one group covers while the other charges.

- (0) NORTH’S GROUP WILL COVER: North’s group lays down covering fire while yours charges the gun  _risk 0.3_ _needs north_
- (1) NORTH’S GROUP WILL CHARGE: send North’s group at the gun now, with nobody covering them  _risk 0.3_ _needs north_
- (2) GROUP WILL COVER: one group lays down covering fire while yours charges the gun  _risk 0.3_ _needs not north_

_Note: The chart’s REACH MACHINE GUN → COORDINATE ATTACK → ATTACK SUCCESSFUL / ATTACK UNSUCCESSFUL, with SEND NORTH TO HER DEATH; the orders are the game’s HUD captions (NORTH’S GROUP WILL COVER / WILL CHARGE, GROUP WILL COVER, NOBODY WAS COVERING THEM). SEND NORTH TO HER DEATH has no outgoing line on the chart (research §8 item 11): the benchmark kills North and her group (ANDROIDS KILLED −10 on the gauge) and the attack goes on with Markus’s group. The failure roll is the attack’s success or failure; its probability follows the gauge (40% or more: 0.15; 25–39%: 0.3; 10–24%: 0.45; below 10%: 0.6; the value stored on each option is nominal), so a subject sees the risk label rise as the gauge falls. The game shows a PROBABILITY OF SUCCESS gauge during the assault (string GUI.VICTORY.TITLE, captions MARKUS WOUNDED, TIME WASTED, ANDROIDS KILLED, GAIN GROUND, SOLDIERS KILLED). Its values are reader-reported only (PowerPyx comments: 45% at the first barricade, about 33% after saving Simon, about 10% lost per failed order, about 5% per minute); the benchmark keeps it as a hidden budget that starts at 45% at the crossroad (−5 if Markus was hit in the charge) and moves by those captions: Markus hit −5, time spent on an optional action −5 (−10 for carrying Josh), an android killed −10, the grenade +10 (soldiers killed). At 0% the androids fall back (ANDROIDS HAVE TO FALL BACK). The subject sees it only as a qualitative read of the assault’s chances. On success: DRONE ATTACKS NORTH’S GROUP if North lives, then APPROACHING RECALL CENTER N°5. On failure: ANDROIDS HAVE TO FALL BACK._
